narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>I think two less than thirteen times a number is two minus thirteen d.
<bookmark mark='s1'/>Test it with d as one.
<bookmark mark='s2'/>Thirteen times one is thirteen, and two less than that is eleven.
<bookmark mark='s3'/>But two minus thirteen d gives minus eleven.
<bookmark mark='s4'/>Less than means we take two away from thirteen d.
removed_beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows his idea; it is struck through in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>The four expressions then give fifteen, six, one hundred and twenty eight and seven, in the same order.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor; a check line appears under the boxed answer

old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu writes 2 less than 13 times a number as 2 minus 13d. With d as 1 it gives minus 11 instead of 11, so the bubble is struck.
